title: Purity of fibres under a finite dominant integral cover
statement: Let S be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme; pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let C and D be integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over S [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let r:D\to C be a finite dominant S-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism; def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Assume that there is an integer n\geq0 such that every nonempty scheme-theoretic fibre C_s [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is pure of dimension n, meaning that every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of C_s has topological Krull dimension n [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then every nonempty fibre D_s is pure of dimension n.

source.place: Dimension-of-fibres discussion using openness of the bounded-dimension locus (02FZ), together with Algebra Tags 00OK and 00OY for finite integral dimension preservation; the proof adds the standard going-up argument that a component of a fibre of a finite dominant integral map maps onto a component downstairs.
